retainedDonorRecord.name: Sirius A
retainedDonorRecord.notes: Sirius system position and physical properties use Bond et al. (2017), including the adopted 378.9 mas parallax. The component offset is below this catalog's spatial precision. Motion: system motion shared by A and B; Hipparcos proper motion (SIMBAD HIP 32349; 2007A&A...474..653V) and true systemic RV -8.47 km/s from Bond et al. (2017) section V.1. No binary orbital motion; Galactic conversion documented in README. Sirius A reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The radius is interferometric, the mass dynamical, and the luminosity and temperature use the adopted parallax. The age and bulk [Fe/H] are stellar-evolution model results; the bulk metallicity is used instead of Sirius A's diffusion-altered Am photospheric abundance. Full classification of Sirius A, including metallic-line morphology; Sirius B is separate.

record.name: Sirius B
record.notes: Sirius system position and white-dwarf properties use Bond et al. (2017). The component offset is below this catalog's spatial precision. Motion: inherited Sirius system motion as for A; Hipparcos proper motion (2007A&A...474..653V) and true systemic RV -8.47 km/s from Bond et al. (2017) section V.1. Not the white dwarf's gravitationally redshifted RV; no binary orbital motion. Sirius B reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The mass is dynamical; temperature, radius, and luminosity come from HST/STIS atmosphere and absolute-flux fitting. The displayed age is the total evolutionary age, not merely the 126 Myr white-dwarf cooling time. Photospheric metallicity remains intentionally blank for this pure-hydrogen white dwarf. retainedDonorRecord.name: Procyon A
retainedDonorRecord.notes: 10pc census (2023-08-25), object 31, system 16; alf CMi A. J2000 Sun-relative Galactic position via Astropy; full-space-motion.   No orbital model. Procyon A component parameters: dynamical mass and preferred 2.70 Gyr high-core-overshoot age from Bond et al. (2015); age is model-dependent (alternative tracks 1.673 and 1.817 Gyr). Chiavassa et al. (2012) provide 6591 +/- 43 K and the 2.019 solar interferometric radius; the alternative bolometric flux gives 6556 +/- 84 K. Photospheric [Fe/H] is the differential 3D LTE result of Allende Prieto et al. (2002). Component-resolved Johnson V=0.34 from 1953ApJ...117..313J; 2015ApJ...813..106B; absolute V uses the adopted distance. luminosity_solar derived by Stefan-Boltzmann scaling from adopted inputs (solar Teff=5772 K); inherits their measurement/model/estimate assumptions. Preserve the existing reviewed component-scoped physical parameters and their published/derived provenance. Primary-only Procyon A classification; the composite F5IV-V+DQZ spectrum is not appropriate for a component A row.
